effects: The signer, as the current controller of the ZK address (EPK) `epk`, lets anyone who holds the signature call changeControllerWithAuth. That call replaces the signer with `newController` in the Hub's controller registry (`controllers[epk] = newController`), so the signer loses control of that ZK address and the new controller gets it.
The signer's authorization nonce `nonce` is used up in the AuthorizationChecker bitmap and cannot be reused.
The signature is only valid while `block.timestamp < deadline`. It is checked with SignatureChecker, so contract wallets (ERC-1271) work too. No tokens or ETH move.
formats.shown: "Set controller to {newController}", with the new controller as a resolved name, the ZK address as raw bytes32 and the deadline as a date. The nonce is not shown.

findings.title: ChangeControllerAuth intent does not say the signer hands over control of their ZK address.
findings.evidence: ZKHub.sol changeControllerWithAuth: `_consumeAuthorization(oldController, digest, auth); controllers[epk] = newController;`, so the signer is the old controller and loses control of the EPK. Descriptor: intent "Change controller", interpolatedIntent "Set controller to {newController}". The EPK only appears as a raw field labelled 'ZK address'. Case 0 screen: "Set controller to Alice".
findings.fix: Make the wording say it is a handover, e.g. intent "Transfer control of your ZK address" and interpolatedIntent "Give control of your ZK address to {newController}".

findings.title: ChangeControllerAuth does not show the nonce. It only prevents replay and moves no assets.
findings.evidence: AuthorizationChecker._useAuthNonce(signer, nonce) sets a bit in the signer's nonce bitmap. The descriptor fields list newController, epk and deadline only.
findings.fix: None needed. A nonce field labelled 'Nonce' could be added if wanted.

findings.title: ChangeControllerAuth shows the ZK address only as a raw 32-byte compressed Grumpkin point.
findings.evidence: Grumpkin.sol `type CompressedPoint is bytes32;`. Descriptor field `epk` 'ZK address' uses format raw. Case 0 shows 0x2020…2020.
findings.fix: No ERC-7730 format renders a compressed curve point better. Keep raw.
